grade_reasons: Consistency: a single meta-analysis / systematic review exists, but its conclusion is not independently replicated or verified — held at moderate.

layers.note: Human evidence present: human certainty sets the overall score.

claims.summary: For testosterone / hormones, Iodine has moderate human evidence (32 studies).

explanation.what_it_is: Iodine is a trace mineral essential for human health, obtained primarily from food and water. It is a core component of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4), which regulate metabolism, growth, and energy production throughout the body.
explanation.how_it_works: Your thyroid gland uses iodine to synthesize thyroid hormones, which control metabolic rate and influence reproductive hormone balance. Adequate iodine availability ensures normal thyroid function; without it, thyroid hormone production declines, disrupting downstream hormonal signaling including effects on testosterone and other sex hormones. This interconnection between thyroid health and hormonal status is why iodine status can influence overall hormonal regulation.

proven_benefits.note: Human evidence from 32 studies supports that adequate iodine intake is associated with healthy testosterone levels and broader hormonal regulation, likely through its role in thyroid function.

explanation.emerging_research: Recent work explores whether iodine status influences other aspects of reproductive and metabolic health beyond testosterone, and whether supplementation in iodine-replete populations offers additional benefits. These directions remain early and require further study.
explanation.caveats: More than adequate iodine intake (exceeding 1,100 μg/day in adults) may worsen thyroid function in sensitive individuals; balance is critical. Iodine requirements are modest and easily met through iodized salt and seafood in most developed regions—supplementation is most relevant in iodine-deficient populations or those with specific dietary restrictions.
